R-009: detection misses JFS, UFS1/2 and ReiserFS.

Deliberately we_write = false. A superfloppy is defined by the ABSENCE of a
partition table, so there is nothing for an oracle to inspect — any filesystem
oracle that reads the volume at offset 0 has already proved it. Listing it as
a write path would manufacture a permanent unfillable gap.

oracles.notes: Four versions present locally (0.174/0.189/0.273/0.288); our output verifies on all four, so the version spread is itself a coverage axis.
macOS only. Nothing equivalent exists elsewhere, which is what makes a Mac non-optional.
Symantec Ghost Explorer 11.5. Windows only; three copies present locally.
Checks Linux-flavoured XFS; IRIX is the authority for SGI XFS.

Linux kernel AFFS driver. Available on the MiSTer's HPS because that
is ARM Linux with affs built in — but this is a LINUX opinion, not an Amiga
one, and is worth exactly what the same mount on any Linux box is worth. The
Amiga's own filesystem code lives in the core; see mister-core-amiga.
Closes the nine-DPB CP/M axis, the largest sub-axis in the suite, for one apt install.
SGI emulator written in Rust; in-house, so blockers are fixable at source. Replaces MAME for IRIX.
Cross-platform Amiga. WinUAE is Windows-only, so this is the portable choice.
OS/2's own CHKDSK is the only real HPFS oracle; the Linux hpfs module is read-only and absent from WSL.

Real AmigaOS reading the volume with its own filesystem handlers.
Unlike the HPS affs mount, this is the Amiga's opinion. Bootable Workbench
1.3 / 2.1 RDB+PFS disks are already on the board.

Real Apple II reading the disk with ProDOS / DOS 3.3 themselves.
/media/fat/games/Apple-II is already populated on the board, so this needs no
new material — it closes two write gaps that had no oracle at all.

Modern Macintosh emulator written in Rust. Emulating a Mac Plus gives
a real MFS implementation — the only realistic judge of MFS, which otherwise
has no oracle anywhere. NB: snowemu.com returned HTTP 403 when checked on
2026-08-02, so confirm the project and its automation surface before the
matrix leans on it.

For our own container formats there is no third party and never will
be, so structural inspection is circular by construction. The honest check is
behavioural: back up a real installed system, restore it, and boot the result.
If the machine still comes up and its files are intact, the format did its job.

Canonical scenario, which also exercises CB-DOS end to end:

  1. Build a small DOS 6.22 VM (QEMU or VMware) and install it bootable.
  2. Back that disk up with rb-cli into cbk.
  3. Restore onto an SD card (or back into a VM disk).
  4. Boot it and assert the guest reaches a prompt with its files intact.

This single case covers more than the container: backup, restore, the CB-DOS
path, partition and boot-sector fidelity, and — when the target is real media
— the hardware write path from HARDWARE.md. Highest coverage-per-case in the
suite, which is why it is worth the setup cost.

Java, so it runs on all three desktop hosts — which is why it is
preferred over the per-OS alternatives (CiderPress on Windows, Applesauce on
macOS). Reads 2MG / DSK / PO / DO and lists ProDOS and DOS 3.3 volumes.
macOS only, but it is the reference implementation for the flux formats.
No PC-98 core exists on the MiSTer, so MAME's pc9801 drivers are the route for HDM and DIM.
Acorn Archimedes; RISC OS reads ADFS with its own FileCore.

Confirmed present on the board. Lisa FS was listed as having no
oracle anywhere — the core is one, and it is the only realistic one.
Windows' own NTFS checker. Relevant to R-007, where a freshly formatted volume fails its own fsck on BackupBootMismatch — chkdsk is the arbiter.
In-kernel NTFS driver; absent from WSL, needs a full Linux host.
Reads MBR, GPT and Sun disk labels. MBR and GPT are the two commonest schemes we write and had no oracle at all until now.
APM is an Apple scheme, so Apple's own tool is the authority.
